items.description: Analyze repository structure and initialize modular concepts
items.acceptance_criteria: Document listing all major modules, their purposes, and initial software project scaffolding

items.description: Literature review via web search on Conway's 99-graph problem
items.acceptance_criteria: Summary document detailing state-of-the-art computational and algebraic approaches to SRG(99,14,1,2)
At least 10 relevant papers cited in sources.bib in the repository root, detailing prior structural bounds and search attempts

items.description: Initialize concept tree for research paths
items.acceptance_criteria: Initial concept tree created in results/concept_evolve/tree/ mapping out algebraic, combinatorial, and computational strategies

items.description: Subagent Delegation: Deep exploration of mathematical constraints
items.acceptance_criteria: Subagent produces a synthesis report detailing eigenvalue multiplicities, Krein bounds, and absolute bounds for SRG(99,14,1,2)
Unit tests passing in CI for validating adjacency matrices of known SRGs (e.g., Petersen, Paley graphs)
Code generating CNF or SMT-LIB files accurately reflecting the graph constraints (A^2 = 14I + A + 2(J-I-A))
Integration of Nauty or Traces library with the baseline solver for symmetry checking and canonical labeling

items.description: Subagent Delegation: Implement baseline metrics tracking
items.acceptance_criteria: Subagent deploys a metric tracking module logging search nodes, execution time, and memory usage into a standardized format
Subroutine that immediately prunes search branches violating Delsarte or Hoffman bounds for cliques/independent sets

items.description: Concept tree evolution: Analyze assumed automorphisms
items.acceptance_criteria: Update results/concept_evolve/tree/ exploring group theory constraints like Z3, Z9, or Z11 actions to reduce search space
SAT/ILP model augmented with Lex-Leader constraints or algebraic symmetry breakers based on assumed automorphisms
Implementation of a stochastic local search, simulated annealing, or tabu search approach operating directly on the adjacency matrix

items.description: Subagent Delegation: Explore construction from smaller geometries
items.acceptance_criteria: Subagent delivers a synthesis report analyzing potential lifts, tactical configurations, or block designs that could yield the 99-graph
Working ILP model implementation (e.g., via Gurobi or CPLEX) modeling the intersection arrays of the SRG

items.description: Execute SAT/SMT baseline on small sub-instances
items.acceptance_criteria: Logs verifying correct and rapid classification of non-existence for intentionally restricted, impossible subgraphs

items.description: Run large-scale search under assumed symmetries
items.acceptance_criteria: Computation logs demonstrating the exhaustive search of at least one major automorphism group branch (e.g., Z11)
Trajectory data and fitness plots comparing the convergence rates of the adjacency matrix approximations over time

items.description: Subagent Delegation: Dynamic bottleneck and conflict analysis
items.acceptance_criteria: Subagent analyzes the solver logs to identify the slowest propagation steps and dynamically suggests refined symmetry-breaking clauses

items.description: Cross-validate bounds via separate solver tracks
items.acceptance_criteria: Independent scripts verifying the exhausted search spaces or cross-checking any generated partial graphs between SAT and ILP formulations
Comprehensive document detailing the exact search spaces exhausted, computational bounds reached, and intermediate graph structures found
A formal section comparing current computational effort, limits, and bounds against the prior work cited in sources.bib
Update to results/concept_evolve/tree/ outlining why the graph likely does or does not exist based on empirical bounds and symmetries explored

items.description: Subagent Delegation: Draft the final research paper
items.acceptance_criteria: Subagent produces a formatted LaTeX document compiling the methodology, bounds, solver configurations, and results into a coherent academic paper
All code is documented, reproducibility scripts are validated in an isolated environment, and the final research_rubric.json is marked completed
